import mir_eval
import numpy as np

# Create deliberately small inputs with the same total duration [0.0, 3.2]
ref_ivs = np.array([[0.0, 2.0], [2.0, 2.5], [2.5, 3.2]])

# 1. Perfect segmentation (identical intervals)
est_ivs_perfect = np.array([[0.0, 2.0], [2.0, 2.5], [2.5, 3.2]])
score_perfect = mir_eval.chord.overseg(ref_ivs, est_ivs_perfect)

# 2. Oversegmentation (more estimated segments than reference segments)
est_ivs_over = np.array([[0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0], [2.0, 2.5], [2.5, 3.2]])
score_over = mir_eval.chord.overseg(ref_ivs, est_ivs_over)

# Verify the documented contract: 1.0 means no oversegmentation
assert score_perfect == 1.0, f"Expected 1.0 for identical intervals, got {score_perfect}"
assert 0.0 <= score_over < 1.0, f"Expected < 1.0 for oversegmented intervals, got {score_over}"

print(f"__CHECK__ overseg {score_perfect}, {score_over:.3f}")
